sources.entry: paho-mqtt - The Eclipse Paho MQTT client for Python.

summary.one_liner: The Eclipse Paho MQTT client library for Python, providing a full MQTT client plus simple publish/subscribe helper functions.
summary.what_it_does: Implements MQTT protocol versions 5.0, 3.1.1 and 3.1 for Python 3.9+. The Client class connects to an MQTT broker, subscribes to topics, receives and publishes messages, and exposes callbacks for connect, disconnect, message, publish, subscribe and log events. Network processing can be driven by a threaded loop (loop_start/loop_stop), a blocking loop_forever(), a manual loop(), or an external event loop using loop_read/loop_write/loop_misc and socket callbacks (examples mention asyncio and select). The paho.mqtt.publish and paho.mqtt.subscribe modules offer one-shot helpers (single, multiple, simple, callback). A topic_matches_sub() helper checks whether a topic matches a subscription pattern. Callback API is versioned via CallbackAPIVersion, with VERSION2 recommended.
use_cases: publish sensor readings to an MQTT broker
subscribe to IoT device topics in Python
send one-off MQTT messages from a script
integrate MQTT with asyncio or select-based applications
check whether an MQTT topic matches a wildcard subscription
troubleshoot MQTT connections with logging callbacks
how_to_run: git clone the repository and run: pip install -e . (from the paho.mqtt.python folder)
import paho.mqtt.client as mqtt; from paho.mqtt.enums import CallbackAPIVersion
notable: Versioned callback API (CallbackAPIVersion.VERSION2 recommended) with reason codes and properties for MQTT 5.x
Multiple network loop options: threaded loop_start, blocking loop_forever, manual loop, or external event loop support
Built-in one-shot publish and subscribe helper modules
Part of the Eclipse Foundation Paho project
caveats: Known limitation: with clean_session=False the session is only kept in memory, so QoS 1/2 state is lost on process restart and messages may be lost
With clean_session=True, QoS>0 messages are republished on reconnect, which the README admits is not standard-compliant and can allow duplicate QoS 2 delivery
Release 2.0 contains breaking changes; see migration notes. CallbackAPIVersion.VERSION1 is deprecated and slated for removal in 3.0
